own_scenes.place: San Francisco, Berkeley y Los Ángeles
own_scenes.desc: A principios de 1966 había distritos psicodélicos con locales, grupos, ropa, impresos y drogas propios en Londres, Los Ángeles y San Francisco. Los Merry Pranksters de Ken Kesey convirtieron su desafío «Can You Pass the Acid Test?» en fiestas de luces, cine y sonido grabado y devuelto al instante: la segunda, en San José en diciembre de 1965 tras un concierto de los Stones, y nueve más en los tres primeros meses de 1966 (cinco en Los Ángeles, una en Watts). Los beats se habían mudado de North Beach a Haight-Ashbury; los Thelin abrieron la Psychedelic Shop y con Stewart Brand se hizo el Trips Festival (6.000 personas). La banda sonora era Rubber Soul. El caos sustituía al cuidado de Leary por el «set and setting»: en el Acid Test de Watts, Ken Babbs amplificó por micrófono los gritos de una chica en pleno mal viaje.

notes.chapter: Septiembre: 7 And 7 Is: provocaciones, sombras y un nuevo lenguaje
notes.text: En el verano de 1966 la ciudad era un hervidero de grupos, salas y actitudes: el Fillmore de Bill Graham y la Family Dog de Chet Helms, salas grandes con reverberación, pósteres alucinógenos, improvisaciones modales y un look bohemio de vaqueros y chaquetas militares. Ralph J. Gleason, desde el Chronicle, fue su gran valedor y prefería a los grupos de raíz folk e improvisación (Grateful Dead, Jefferson Airplane) a los rockeros adolescentes. Antes habían salido los Beau Brummels y el R&B de Autumn Records con Sly Stone de productor. The Great!! Society!! de Grace Slick estiraba «Someone to Love» y «White Rabbit» en el Matrix; Big Brother estrenaba a Janis Joplin; Jefferson Airplane Takes Off fue la primera declaración coherente de la escena, «quizá el mejor disco de rock jamás producido» según Sculatti. Al otro lado de la bahía, Berkeley ponía la parte activista: Jerry Rubin se presentó vestido de soldado de la Guerra de Independencia ante el Comité de Actividades Antiamericanas.

notes.chapter: Octubre: Winchester Cathedral: tiempo pasado, presente y futuro
notes.text: El 16 de octubre Grace Slick cantó por primera vez con Jefferson Airplane; Big Brother sacó su primer single, «Blind Man», con «All Is Loneliness» de Moondog en la cara B, un dron con la voz rasposa de Janis Joplin. «Algo va a pasar», decía ella. Los grupos tocaban en parques y salones de baile y eso dio a su sonido una amplitud de frontera.

notes.chapter: Diciembre: My Mind’s Eye: sueños de libertad, una minoría profética y el regreso a la infancia
notes.text: En diciembre Haight-Ashbury llegaba a la masa crítica: «la comunidad más avanzada que conozco», decía Richard Alpert; música de drogas para públicos drogados, con los grupos como guías psicodélicos y una escena total de grupos, luces, pósteres y salas. Gleason habló de la «Love Generation». Pero crecían las tensiones: metedrina, la guerra entre Chet Helms y Bill Graham, los Diggers contra todos («el amor no es un concierto con luces a 3 dólares»), su desfile por la muerte del dinero el 17 de diciembre y el asalto a la comisaría. En Nochevieja Moby Grape cerró en el Avalon con «Dark Magic», diecisiete minutos de improvisación.

influences.name: Berkeley y la protesta contra la guerra

refs.q: By the beginning of 1966, there were psychedelic districts in several major cities
refs.para: By the beginning of 1966, there were psychedelic districts in several major cities – London, Los Angeles and San Francisco, in particular – all of which had their own venues, their own groups and their own subcultures based around clothes, print, music and drugs. The traditional youthful artistic desire to create one’s own world was heightened by LSD. No drug before or since has driven such a wedge between those who partook and those who did not.
refs.chapter: Abril: The Third Eye: el LSD y sus descontentos

refs.q: The word was spreading. On the West Coast, the Merry Pranksters held a series of nine Acid Tests in the first three months of 1966.
refs.para: The word was spreading. On the West Coast, the Merry Pranksters held a series of nine Acid Tests in the first three months of 1966. There were five in Los Angeles, dotted around the city in Northridge, Hollywood and, bizarrely, Watts – still highly unsettled after the disastrous riots. At the same time, teen nightspots began to mushroom out from the traditional Sunset Strip base: as well as Elmer Valentine’s The Trip (opened in late 1965), the new clubs had psychedelic, Huxleyan names like the Brave New World or the Doors of Perception.
refs.chapter: Abril: The Third Eye: el LSD y sus descontentos

refs.q: By September 1966, Haight-Ashbury was shaping up as another youthtopia.
refs.para: By September 1966, Haight-Ashbury was shaping up as another youthtopia. Like the Sunset Strip, the area had been blighted for well over a decade by planned highway development, and it afforded cheap and liveable housing near the centre of the city. The architecture was late-Victorian, and the atmosphere relaxed and spacious: Haight Street stopped at the eastern end of Golden Gate Park, with the Panhandle stretching in parallel for several blocks.
refs.chapter: Septiembre: 7 And 7 Is: provocaciones, sombras y un nuevo lenguaje

refs.q: By late summer, San Francisco was making waves with the nationwide release of Jefferson Airplane Takes Off.
refs.para: By late summer, San Francisco was making waves with the nationwide release of Jefferson Airplane Takes Off. One of the first SF groups, Jefferson Airplane had signed a contract with RCA Records in late 1965 and had released a couple of flop folk rock singles, ‘It’s No Secret’ and ‘Come Up the Years’. Delayed by RCA, who objected to the use of the word ‘trips’ in a song called ‘Runnin’ Around This World’, the album was the scene’s first coherent statement.
refs.chapter: Septiembre: 7 And 7 Is: provocaciones, sombras y un nuevo lenguaje

refs.para: Joplin was a compelling performer. Her voice sliced through the group’s Sturm und Drang, while her vulnerability was well hidden under a tough facade. By October, Big Brother were one of the leading groups on the scene. ‘The audience is getting bigger and bigger,’ bassist David Getz told Mojo Navigator, ‘there’s really no limit to how big this thing could become, in this country.’ Joplin was more direct: ‘Something’s gonna happen. It isn’t just gonna go on. Something’s gonna happen. Either we’re all gonna go broke and split up, or get rich and famous.’
refs.chapter: Octubre: Winchester Cathedral: tiempo pasado, presente y futuro

refs.q: The Love Generation: it was a very powerful idea, and reflective of the mood in San Francisco that winter.
refs.para: The Love Generation: it was a very powerful idea, and reflective of the mood in San Francisco that winter. It wasn’t the full story, however. Haight-Ashbury had started small but was swelling day by day, week by week, and the tensions were growing. The Oracle ran a piece about methedrine abuse in the city. Chet Helms at the Avalon was busy arguing with Bill Graham at the Fillmore, who had banned Mojo Navigator from the venue. The Diggers hated the Oracle as ‘an old cunt rag of misinformation, outdated “news”, fey psychedelic bullshit art’.
refs.chapter: Diciembre: My Mind’s Eye: sueños de libertad, una minoría profética y el regreso a la infancia

refs.q: The word was Love but the shadow was Hate.
refs.para: The word was Love but the shadow was Hate. Gleason was determined to present the positive side of the San Francisco scene, but the actuality wasn’t always up to the ideal. What with The Love Book arrests, the regular problems at Diggers street events and constantly hostile policing, Haight-Ashbury felt under attack. In December, the Oracle canvassed its readers for ‘written reports with dates, names and badges’ for a portfolio on police harassment, illegal searches and the like.
refs.chapter: Diciembre: My Mind’s Eye: sueños de libertad, una minoría profética y el regreso a la infancia
